column3: Create a reproducible F# Console Application targeting .NET Framework 4.7.2 and an F# Class Library targeting .NET Standard 2.0; open the solution in Visual Studio Insiders; verify IntelliSense proposes the library namespace; rebuild successfully; debug to a breakpoint and validate console output; then inspect the Application and Build property pages.

column4: Resolve the current user's home directory.
Open a command prompt for deterministic project setup.
Bring the setup command prompt to the foreground.
Remove the fixed project directory from any previous run and report whether cleanup succeeded.

column16: The fixed project directory is clean.

column4: Write the FSharpLibrary project file targeting .NET Standard 2.0.
Write the library implementation used by the console project.
column6:
["--out", "{vars.home}\ui-auto-fsharp-multi\FSharpLibrary\Library.fs", "--text", "namespace FSharpLibrary

module Say =
    let hello name = printfn "Hello %s" name
"]

column4: Write the FSharpConsole project file targeting .NET Framework 4.7.2 with a project reference.
Write the initial console program before the IntelliSense edit.
column6:
["--out", "{vars.home}\ui-auto-fsharp-multi\FSharpConsole\Program.fs", "--text", "open System

[<EntryPoint>]
let main argv =
    printfn "Hello world from F#"
    0
"]

column4: Return focus to the setup command prompt.
Create the solution add the executable project first and restore dependencies.
column6: ["cd /d \"{vars.home}\\ui-auto-fsharp-multi\" && dotnet new sln -n FSharpMultiProject --format sln --force && dotnet sln FSharpMultiProject.sln add \"FSharpConsole\\FSharpConsole.fsproj\" \"FSharpLibrary\\FSharpLibrary.fsproj\" && dotnet restore FSharpMultiProject.sln --source https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json && echo SETUP_COMPLETE>\"{vars.home}\\ui-auto-fsharp-setup-{timestamp}.ready\"", "--interval", "0.001"]
column16: FSharpConsole is the default startup project and the solution is restored.

column4: Wait for solution creation and package restore to complete.
column16: The solution and both projects are ready.

column4: Launch the fixed solution in Visual Studio Insiders.
column17: The solution opens in Visual Studio Insiders.

column4: Find the collapsed FSharpConsole project in Solution Explorer.
Wait for Program.fs to appear in Solution Explorer.
Locate the active Visual Studio code editor.
Click the code editor to give it keyboard focus.

column16: Caret moved to the first statement in main.

column4: Move to the start of the line.

Paste the namespace prefix into the editor.
Open Visual Studio List Members without using the IME-reserved Ctrl+Space shortcut.

column16: IntelliSense closed and temporary prefix removed.

column4: Put the complete indented library call on the clipboard.
Paste the complete library call as the first statement in main.
Wait until the Visual Studio status bar reports a successful rebuild.

column4: Return focus to the code editor.
Enter line 7 containing the return value.

column4: Set a breakpoint on the return line.
Wait for the FSharpConsole window and capture its handle.
